solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Horny old beast put in A&E by one serving unbeatably on team?

indicators.note: put in A&E says the answer sits between an A and an E, so the wordplay is the answer with those letters around it and they must be stripped off

parts.note: an acer serves aces that cannot be returned, on is atop, and a team is a side: ACER ATOP SIDE

explanation.surface: A prehistoric beast lands in casualty after a tennis player on a team hits it.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E looks like the hospital department, but 'put in A&E' means the answer goes between the letters A and E, so the server, on and team pieces are the answer with an A at the front and an E at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceratopsid is a horned dinosaur such as Triceratops, an ancient creature with horns.

clue.text: Gem cut at top and six-pack comprising Mike's dearest possessions

indicators.note: cut at top says the first letter is removed, the top in a down clue

parts.note: a jewel is a gem

indicators.note: comprising means containing, so the six-pack holds the radio letter

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, abs
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Mike's most treasured things are a cut gem and his toned stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: JEWEL loses its top to give EWEL, and ABS takes in M. The phrase comes from Nathan's parable of the poor man's one ewe lamb in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a figurative term for one's most treasured possession, after the biblical parable.

clue.text: Sweet-tasting fish a second person starved of oxygen

indicators.note: starved of means deprived of, so the oxygen letter is removed

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone eats a sweet fish while short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The ayu is a small Japanese river fish, also called sweetfish for its sweet flesh.

clue.text: Raise grand in shared currency for multibarrelled shooter

indicators.note: raise means lift, so in a down clue the whole is turned to read upwards
in says the grand letter goes inside the currency word

parts.note: the euro is the currency shared by many European countries
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A call to raise a thousand in euros to buy a big gun.
explanation.walkthrough: G inside EURO makes EUGRO, and 'Raise' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgue was an old weapon with many gun barrels fired together, like organ pipes.

clue.text: Ancient form of document left in county to the north and east

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside
to the north means upwards in a down clue, so the county is read backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: An old document was left in a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns the county abbreviation upwards in this down clue, and 'in' slips the left letter between it and the east letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrowle is an old form of scroll, a rolled-up written document.

clue.text: Creator god protects fighter circling Sumerian city

indicators.note: protects means shields, so the god word surrounds the rest

parts.note: deus is Latin for god

indicators.note: circling says the fighter goes round the city

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
Ur was an ancient city of Sumer in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A deity shields a warplane as it circles an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creator god' looks like one phrase but splits: Creator is the definition, god gives DEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic philosophy the demiurge or demiurgus is the maker of the world, so a creator.

clue.text: Islamic judge's bit of publicity in show of surprising facts

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads 'Islamic judge is'

indicators.note: in says the publicity goes inside the show

parts.note: QI is a British TV quiz show built around odd facts
an ad is a bit of publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A Muslim judge is advertised on a quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a BBC panel show of obscure trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: A qadi is a judge in a sharia court, applying Islamic law.

clue.text: Ruler used to circumscribe radius and clip one's beak

indicators.note: used to circumscribe means made to surround, so the ruler goes around everything else

parts.note: a queen is a ruler
to cuff is to clip, as in a clip round the ear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monarch measures a circle and strikes someone's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEEN surrounds R, CUFF and I. Beak is British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer cuffin is old thieves' cant for a justice of the peace, a magistrate or beak.

clue.text: Aperitif, extremely fine to be imbibed by thirsty good-for-nothing

indicators.note: to be imbibed by means drunk in, so these letters go inside the thirsty word

parts.note: dry means thirsty

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of aperitif
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A thirsty layabout downs a fine aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' keeps just the ends of 'Aperitif'; with the fine letter, they are 'imbibed by' the thirsty word, sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Draffy is an old word for worthless, like draff, the dregs left after brewing.

clue.text: Begrudge developing tool for improving software

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of begrudge take a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone resents building a programming aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' looks like software jargon, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debugger is a program used to find and remove errors in code.

clue.text: Old lady recalled European woman frequenting orgies

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady in slang

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the European is read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European, from Denmark

explanation.surface: A mother remembers a Danish woman who went to wild parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus at his orgiastic rites.

clue.text: Australian nipper back in the same place in auction site

indicators.note: back says the whole is read in reverse
in says the same-place letters go inside the auction site

parts.note: eBay is an online auction site
ib is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: An Australian child is back where they were, on an auction website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like a child but is a crustacean with nippers. The second 'in' places the ibidem letters after the auction site's first letter, and 'back' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A yabbie is an Australian freshwater crayfish, a creature with pincers.

clue.text: Board accepting bit of work on school drive's deep crack in ice

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so board holds the other pieces

parts.note: BD is the abbreviation for board
an erg is a unit of work in physics, set on top of SCH, the abbreviation for school, in this down clue
to run is to drive, as in run a car

explanation.surface: A board accepts a piece of homework about a school outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bergschrund is the deep crevasse where a glacier pulls away from the rock above it.

clue.text: Hostilities engulfing Britain whenever English and Scottish on the alert

definitions.note: the definition names a Scots word meaning wakeful or watchful

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing, so the war word surrounds Britain

parts.note: war is a state of hostilities
UK is the United Kingdom, Britain
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, I stay in'

explanation.surface: Britain at war has to stay alert whether English or Scottish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish' marks the answer as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waukrife is Scots for wakeful or watchful, unable to sleep.

clue.text: Honour someone striking gold with gram in Bavarian village

parts.note: an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
a rammer is someone who rams, strikes
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gold prospector in a German village receives an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberammergau is the Bavarian village famous for its passion play, staged every ten years.

clue.text: Greek character following more commendable Echo is captured by Castor

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp 6f

indicators.note: is captured by says the Echo letter goes inside the commendable word

parts.note: finer means better, more worthy of praise
Echo is E in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure follows Echo captured by the twin Castor of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Castor looks like the mythical twin, but it is a variant spelling of caster, a sugar shaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffineer is a castor for sprinkling sugar or spice on muffins.

clue.text: Boyfriend has local cheat to carry a torch

indicators.note: has says one piece goes with the other, the boyfriend after the cheat

parts.note: flam is a dialect word for a trick or cheat
a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: A woman still carries a torch for a cheating boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry a torch' suggests unrequited love, but the torch is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one carried in a procession.

clue.text: Careful with sauce covering paper and disinfectant doing the same

indicators.note: covering says the sauce goes around the other letters

parts.note: soy is a sauce
the FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
Lysol is a disinfectant; doing the same means it also covers the paper, giving LYSO FT L

explanation.surface: Mind out with the sauce spilt on the newspaper, and with the disinfectant too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the same' means the disinfectant also covers a copy of the paper; that nest follows the paper inside the sauce, which is 'covering' everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Softly-softly describes a cautious approach, so it means careful.

clue.text: Salyut's middle level involves senior Soviet scientist

indicators.note: involves means includes, so senior goes inside
the middle of a six-letter word is its third and fourth letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of Salyut
to KO someone is to knock them out, flatten or level them
SEN is the abbreviation for senior

explanation.surface: The Soviet space station's central floor holds an older cosmonaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Salyut was a Soviet space station. KO as level means to floor someone; 'involves' puts the senior abbreviation between the station's middle and the knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Trofim Lysenko was a Soviet biologist whose discredited genetics was imposed by Stalin.

clue.text: Sodden chamber giving nonstop pain

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
achy describes a constant dull pain

explanation.surface: A waterlogged room causes endless aches.
explanation.walkthrough: A po is a British chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Poachy is a dialect word for wet and spongy ground, sodden underfoot.

clue.text: Foot bones start to hurt less when November's gone

parts.note: sawbones is slang for a doctor, DOC for short

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of hurt

indicators.note: November is N in the radio alphabet, so this removes that letter

parts.note: minus means less

explanation.surface: Foot bones start to hurt less after November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot bones' reads as one phrase, but 'Foot' is the definition, a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dochmius is a metrical foot of five syllables in Greek verse.

clue.text: Gum resin mastic on images' frames

indicators.note: frames means encloses, so the words surround the answer

parts.note: the last letter of mastic, all of on and the first three letters of images

explanation.surface: Mastic, a gum resin, is spread on the frames of pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across masti-C ON IMA-ges; 'mastic' is itself a resin, a neat decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Conima is a fragrant gum resin from a tropical American tree.

clue.text: Modern dance clubs with revolutionary ending in popular music

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the ending is reversed

parts.note: -core is a suffix in pop genre names such as hardcore and grindcore

explanation.surface: Nightclubs play a new dance track with a radical finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceroc is a partner dance developed in 1980s London from jive and salsa.

clue.text: Bulk needing one to change to vineyard's disused press

indicators.note: change to means swap, so the letter for one gives way to the vineyard word

parts.note: bulk is size
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cru is a vineyard, as in grand cru

explanation.surface: A large old wine press needs one part replacing at the vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruze is an obsolete word for squeeze or press, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Secure what holds edges of railing for water pipe

indicators.note: holds says the secure and what words hold the edges between them

parts.note: to nail is to secure
eh is an exclamation meaning what?

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of railing

explanation.surface: Fixing something to grip the ends of a rail for plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' gives the exclamation EH, not a question word; 'holds' has the secure word and it enclose the 'edges of' railing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargileh is a hookah, a pipe that draws tobacco smoke through water.

clue.text: Ruling party members regularly rejected Zionism

indicators.note: regularly rejected means every other letter thrown out, keeping the rest

parts.note: the even-numbered letters of Zionism

explanation.surface: Members of the governing party periodically disowned Zionism.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters Z, O, I, M and keep I, N, S.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins are those in power, the members of the governing party as opposed to the outs.

clue.text: Crossbar in support of millstone's outer edge's sound

indicators.note: sound means said aloud, so the outer-edge word is heard as the answer

parts.note: a rind is the outer layer or edge of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A millstone's iron bar is sound right to the rim.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is pronounced like RIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A rynd is the iron cross-piece that supports the upper millstone on its spindle.

clue.text: Gardening charity crossing over here to Nancy with shady evergeen climber

indicators.note: crossing says the charity letters reach across the others, enclosing them

parts.note: the RHS is the Royal Horticultural Society, a British gardening charity
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ici is French for here, and Nancy is a French city
sus is slang for suspicious, shady

explanation.surface: A gardening charity crosses to France with a shade-loving climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is the French city, so 'here' in French. The clue's 'evergeen' is printed so in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoicissus is a genus of evergreen climbing vines from Africa, grown as house plants.
